examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)

meanings.en: other forms: его (gen/acc), ему (dat), им (instr), нём (prep)

meanings.note: Used as an verbal verb meaning 'to fine, penalize'.

examples.trans: The chef will fine the cooks.

examples.text: Если рыба останется, я вас оштрафую!
examples.trans: If fish remains, I will fine you!

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'deport'.

examples.text: Это слово «депортировать» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'deport' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: думать о + prepositional = to think about

examples.trans: I have no time to think about that.

examples.text: Мне некогда об этом думать. Слишком много дел.
examples.trans: I have no time to think about that. There's too much to do.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine

meanings.en: other forms: этого, этому, это, этим, этом

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('other, another, different').

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.en: to agree, to come to an arrangement

examples.text: Позвони мне вечером. Договоримся на завтра.
examples.trans: Call me this evening. We'll arrange something for tomorrow.

meanings.en: to turn out well, to succeed, to manage (impersonal + dative)
meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'даться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to succeed, to manage', paired with 'удаваться'.

examples.text: Я не поняла, как тебе это удалось.
examples.trans: I didn't understand how you managed that.
And did you manage to find a room?
All right, here you go. There, look.

хотя.gloss: even if, at least (with бы); although

meanings.note: нужно хотя бы поговорить = we need at least to talk

examples.text: Нужно хотя бы поговорить с ними.
examples.trans: We need at least to talk with them.

examples.text: Вы плохо поступили, но хотя бы совесть есть.
examples.trans: You acted badly, but at least you have a conscience.

meanings.note: condition: если хочешь = if you want; а если нет? = and if not?
Common feminine noun meaning 'life' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Эдуард Владимирович, я на минуточку. Я спасла монастырь!
examples.trans: Eduard Vladimirovich, I'll only be a minute. I saved the monastery!

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тульчик'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'little chair, stool' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Это слово «стульчик» часто звучит в разговоре.
examples.trans: This word 'little chair' is often heard in conversation.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
